solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Guide usually helpful when Tom was in charge?

definitions.meaning: a rough practical guideline that generally works
read literally, the reign of Tom Thumb, the tiny hero of the English fairy tale

explanation.surface: A question about some handy guidance from the era when a man called Tom ran things.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb is a thumb-sized boy from English folklore; the period when he was in charge would be his rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough guide based on experience rather than exact measurement is the idiom's everyday meaning.

clue.text: Someone stepping up for review

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a pacer is someone who steps or paces along

explanation.surface: A person promoted from the ranks so as to assess something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses PACER in this down light; 'stepping up' looks like promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A summary going back over the main points is a short review.

clue.text: Ray brewed amber ales

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients up, so the letters of these words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Ray made some pale ales in a homebrew kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name; it is a beam of light. 'brewed' rearranges AMBER ALES.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow concentrated beam of coherent light is a kind of ray.

clue.text: Criminal gaoled for life, finally

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A criminal is locked away for life at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges GAOLED; 'gaoled for life' looks like a sentence, but 'life, finally' is the last stage of a lifetime.
explanation.definitionFit: The final period of a person's life is their later years, the elderly stage.

clue.text: Source of free drink tramps used regularly

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter of the word tramps is used

explanation.surface: Homeless people make regular use of a place offering drinks without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used regularly' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of 'tramps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Water from a faucet costs nothing, so the faucet is a source of a free drink.

clue.text: Disturb snake in hollow underground voluntarily?

indicators.note: in places the jumbled snake inside the hollowed-out word
a hollow word has its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters of underground
disturbing moves things around, so the letters of the word snake are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone disturbs a snake in a hole in the ground, of their own accord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow underground' leaves UD; 'Disturb' turns SNAKE into NASKE, which goes 'in' it. The question mark flags that 'unasked' only loosely means voluntarily.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without being requested implies doing it of your own free will.

clue.text: Feature of healthy regime, hung parliament?

definitions.meaning: an eating plan with the right mix of food groups is part of a healthy lifestyle
a diet is also an assembly or parliament, and one evenly split is balanced

explanation.surface: Asks what a healthy routine and an evenly divided parliament have in common.
explanation.walkthrough: A Diet is a legislative assembly (as in Japan's Diet); a hung parliament, with no majority, is evenly balanced.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensible eating plan with proper proportions of nutrients is central to a healthy routine.

clue.text: Romance narrative's following latest trends

parts.note: a relation is a narrative or account, and the 's adds an S
hip means fashionable, following the latest trends

explanation.surface: A love story's narrative follows what is currently fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a love affair, which is a kind of close personal bond between two people.

clue.text: Former copper speeds regularly, getting let off

parts.note: ex- means former
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word speeds

explanation.surface: An ex-policeman caught speeding repeatedly escapes punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal; 'regularly' takes S, E, D from 'speeds'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be let off is to be released from a duty or penalty, i.e. pardoned.

clue.text: Fine specimen left on fruit tree

indicators.note: on means placed after, as the letter follows the tree in an across light

parts.note: a pear is a fruit tree

explanation.surface: A good example of a plant is left on the orchard tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prized and excellent of its kind is called a gem or jewel, as in a pearl among men.

clue.text: A box American filled with silver spears

indicators.note: filled with puts the silver inside the box-plus-American pair

parts.note: to spar is to box
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A boxing American's gear is stuffed with silver spears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spears' looks like weapons but means the vegetable's shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: The edible shoots of this vegetable are sold as spears.

clue.text: Eat this with grated parmesan, initially tangled together?

definitions.text: Eat this with grated parmesan, initially tangled together?

indicators.note: tangled strands are jumbled, so these letters are mixed into a new order
initially takes the opening letters of grated and parmesan

explanation.surface: A serving suggestion: eat this tangled pasta with grated parmesan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives G and P; with EAT THIS, 'tangled together' rearranges them. The whole clue also describes the pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Long tangled strands of pasta are often eaten topped with grated parmesan.

clue.text: Family showing consideration, except for daughter

indicators.note: except for means take this letter away

parts.note: kind means showing consideration

explanation.surface: Relatives being thoughtful, apart from one daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: One's relatives collectively are one's family members.

clue.text: Some whippets nicely going round together on walk

indicators.note: going round means the run of letters is turned to read backwards
some means only a portion of the letters in whippets nicely is taken

explanation.surface: Several dogs nicely circle together on their walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes PETSNI from 'whippets nicely' and 'going round' turns it back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Marching in step means walking with matching paces, moving together.

clue.text: Champion ahead in game

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a sport is a game
up means ahead, as in being up in a match

explanation.surface: A winner leading in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' is a verb here: to champion something is to back it.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to back or advocate for it.

clue.text: Unhappy doing nothing, one must get out of seat

parts.note: sad means unhappy

indicators.note: get out of means the letter leaves the word

parts.note: idle means doing nothing
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A miserable layabout must be forced out of their chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider sits on this, so it is a seat on a horse or bicycle.

clue.text: Leaders in education suck according to students' work

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of the words education and suck

parts.note: says means according to, as in 'the forecast says'

explanation.surface: A complaint that schooling is rubbish, so say the pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Students write these compositions as coursework.

clue.text: Pinch a little Scotch, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to squeeze sharply between finger and thumb
a small measure of spirits such as whisky

explanation.surface: Steal a drop of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tot of spirits is a dram; also a sharp squeeze of skin.

clue.text: Teacher had to take PE with the wrong form

parts.note: Miss is a schoolchild's name for a female teacher

indicators.note: to take puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: PE stands for physical education, as written

explanation.surface: The teacher had to run a PE lesson with the wrong class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' suggests a school class but means shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deformed has the wrong shape or outline.

clue.text: Colourful finish hurt gymnast's foot

parts.note: pain is hurt

indicators.note: foot means the bottom letter of gymnast's in a down light, its last letter

explanation.surface: A gymnast hurts a foot at the end of a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat applied as a decorative coloured surface coating.

clue.text: Commotion which people heard outside in Havana

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: who means which people

indicators.note: outside means the outer letters of Havana

explanation.surface: Someone heard a disturbance outside in Havana.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuss or uproar is informally called a to-do.

clue.text: Heading for adversity, turn back

indicators.note: heading means the first letter of adversity

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in 'your go'

explanation.surface: Facing hardship, someone turns round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn back' reads as one phrase, but 'turn' is GO and 'back' (in the past) is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Years back means years in the past, earlier.

clue.text: Wrongly sat to use bicycle? How should cyclists sit?

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters of sat are put in an incorrect order

parts.note: to ride is to use a bicycle

explanation.surface: Someone sat badly on a bike and asks the right posture.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with a leg either side is how a rider sits on a saddle.

clue.text: Patrick's one for the Irish, not partisan otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged differently, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: St Patrick serves Ireland without taking sides.
explanation.definitionFit: St Patrick is the holy protector associated with Ireland.
